question.problem:
$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,-2)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{{x}^{5}}, & \,x\ge 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=-2]$ given that the conditional probability density function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,-2)$ is shown above and the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{X|-2}=\frac{4}{3}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=-2] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,-2)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{4}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }4{x}^{-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[4\cdot \frac{{x}^{-2}}{(-2)}]}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & ={[-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}]}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =0-(-2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=-2] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=-2]-{\mu }_{X|-2}^{2} \\  & =2-{(\frac{4}{3})}^{2} \\  & =2-\frac{16}{9} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
